scores.description: Self-reported frequency for this achievement-group context; more frequent is not automatically better teaching.

interpretations.headline: 结果说明
interpretations.interpretation:
This profile describes how often you report using these strategies for the selected Low to Below Average Achieving group. The 0–5 mean follows the source response categories; it is not a percentage, a norm, a measure of student ability, or a rating of teaching quality. A larger value means greater reported frequency, not that every strategy should be used more often.

If a practice already helps pupils learn, identify one piece of work that shows what helped. If implementation feels difficult, consider readiness, curriculum requirements, time and available support before choosing a small adjustment. Frequency alone cannot tell whether an activity was effective.

guidance.text: Recall one recent task for this group. What did pupils say or produce, and what support was available?
Select one upcoming question and plan one follow-up that asks pupils to explain their reasoning.

limitations: The source has 40 strategies across three achievement-group columns; this is one selected subscale and column. Standalone layout and local use have not been separately validated.
No norms or performance thresholds. No total across dimensions or achievement groups. More frequent use is not automatically appropriate or effective.
The source gives no missing-item threshold. This project conservatively reports a mean only for a complete selected subscale; missing or not-applicable is never zero.
Original English content, not a validated Chinese instrument. Teachers self-report; this is not an observed classroom quality measure.
